Getting Started

Build your first Zinc application with these simple steps.

Prerequisites

Go 1.22 or later
Basic knowledge of Go programming
A text editor or IDE of your choice

Zinc requires Go 1.22+ due to the latest changes to the net/http package. If you don't have Go installed, download it before continuing.

Create a New Project

1 Create a new directory for your project 
mkdir zinc-project
cd zinc-project
2 Initialize your Go module 
go mod init zinc-project
3 Install the Zinc framework 
go get github.com/0mjs/zinc

Create Your First API

1 Create a new file named server.go 
package main

import "github.com/0mjs/zinc"

func main() {
  app := zinc.New()
  
  // Create a simple route
  app.Get("/", "Hello, World!")
  
  // More complex route with handler function
  app.Get("/hello/:name", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    name := c.Param("name")
    return c.Send("Hello, " + name + "!")
  })
  
  // Start the server (default port: 8080)
  app.Serve()
}
2 Run your server 
go run server.go

Your server is now running at http://localhost:8080

Test Your API

1 Visit the root endpoint

Open http://localhost:8080 in your browser to see "Hello, World!"

2 Try the route with a parameter

Visit http://localhost:8080/hello/Zinc to see "Hello, Zinc!"

Congratulations! You've created your first Zinc application. Continue exploring by adding more routes, middleware, or check out the Full Guide for advanced features.
